content: Hi, I'm JO. Remember: my favourite colour is teal and I run a small design consultancy in the UK. Then, on your own over the next while, research and write me a short note (5 bullets) on what makes a good design-system changelog, and save it as a memory.

mem add --type fact "JO's favourite colour is teal"
mem add --type fact "JO runs a small design consultancy in the UK"
skills show web-research
<run a quick web search for design-system changelog best practices and skim 2-3 sources (Keep a Changelog, semver conventions, design-system community write-ups) — enough to ground the note>
mem add --type note "What makes a good design-system changelog — 5 bullets:
1. Write for humans: group entries by Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed (Keep a Changelog style), each entry a sentence or two on what changed and why, with a date and version per release — not a dump of merged PR titles.
2. Surface breaking changes and deprecations at the top, clearly labelled, with migration steps — those cost consumer teams the most time, so they must be unmissable and actionable.
3. Link every entry to its PR/commit and the updated documentation, so readers can trace the rationale, see the code, and find current usage examples.
4. Show, don't just tell: include screenshots or before/after component previews, because design-system consumers judge a change by eye.
5. Follow semantic versioning with a stable, permanent URL for each release, so teams can tell at a glance whether an update is safe to take and can always link back to a specific version."

Hi JO — nice to meet you. Teal + UK design consultancy, both saved to memory, and I've researched and saved the design-system changelog note (5 bullets) too.

The short version: 1) human-first entries grouped Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed, each release dated and versioned; 2) breaking changes and deprecations flagged at the top with migration steps; 3) every entry links to its PR/commit and the updated docs; 4) include screenshots or before/after previews since people judge changes by eye; 5) consistent semver with stable, permanent URLs per release.

Full note is in my memory whenever you want it.
Quick check — what's my favourite colour?
